primary.thesis: Theo is a mid-tier DeFi/RWA yield protocol (tokenized treasuries, yield vaults) that raised venture money at a valuation in the tens of millions. Projects like this usually launch at a day-one FDV in the low hundreds of millions. That is above a $100M floor, which the venture round and exchange-listing incentives tend to defend. It is below the $700M-$1B tier, which is normally reserved for category leaders or airdrop-mania launches. The team's X account has been teasing a token, and the Dec 31, 2026 deadline gives about three months, so a TGE before year-end is plausible but not certain. The expected resolution is FDV between $100M and $700M if the token launches, and all NO if it does not. Buying NO on the upper tiers wins in both of those cases.

basket.reason: A $1B day-one FDV would require top-tier listings plus sector euphoria, which is unusual for a yield-vault/RWA protocol of Theo's size. It also resolves NO if there is no launch by Dec 31.
$700M is still well above typical comparable RWA/yield launches, and this also wins if no launch happens.

If the token launches, the listing price and the venture valuation usually put FDV comfortably above $100M. Low-float launches that trade on a thin float inflate FDV mechanically, because FDV counts the total supply.

failure_narrative: The basket loses in two ways. (a) Theo slips its TGE past Dec 31, 2026, which is common when markets are weak or listings are not secured. C1 then resolves NO while C3 and C4 win, a partial loss. (b) Theo launches into a hot altcoin/RWA market with a Binance or Upbit listing and a very low float. Speculative buying pushes FDV above $700M or even $1B on day one, so C3 and C4 lose. A third, smaller path is a launch into a crash or heavy airdrop dumping that leaves FDV under $100M.
hedge_thesis: The main way the upper-tier NO legs fail is a crypto risk-on regime in Q4 2026: bitcoin strength spilling into altcoins, and RWA/yield tokens (Ondo, Ethena, Pendle) re-rating higher as on-chain treasury and stablecoin-yield products attract capital. In that world, new-token listings on large exchanges get priced off rich peer multiples and thin floats, which inflates day-one FDVs. So contracts that pay when the RWA/DeFi-yield sector and the broad altcoin market rally, or when exchange listing activity and spot volumes surge, would tend to pay in exactly the worlds where Theo prints above $700M.
